title: Normalized coefficient Weil duality and exceptional-adjunction data
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $D$, distinct primes $\ell$ and $D.p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a separated finite-type model $X_0$ over $D.k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Use the actual finite and common-stage duality and exceptional data of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], their derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and Weil pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Define Duality to record a dualizing Frobenius isomorphism, a natural comparison $P D\cong D P$, its evaluation normalization, and equivariance of dual arrows, evaluation and the actual biduality. The dual structure is $c_K D(\theta_K^{-1})$. Define Exceptional to record left exchange and its inverse-left right mate under the specified adjunction, with equivariance of the same unit and counit. Define DualityComparison and ExceptionalComparison by their componentwise intertwining equations for prescribed scalar or inclusion functors. Coefficients packages these data at every finite coefficient field, their scalar comparisons, and the common-stage data and normalized inclusions. FrobeniusAdjunctions pins left exchange, after conjugation by the specified finite compact-support realizations, to the canonical Frobenius exchange of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], and pins its common-stage components to the canonical descended exchange. Adjunctions additionally imposes the scalar and inclusion intertwining equations. DualizingNormalization requires that the dualizing Frobenius is the normalized structure-morphism mate applied to the coefficient unit, for each model compactification. The fiber wrappers use the actual geometric base change, with inherited finite-type and separatedness proofs. These are definitions, with no assertion that the records are inhabited.
